## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_inventory` retries up to 8 times, which breaks the repository's 3-attempt retry cap, and this must be fixed before merge. The pull request adds the `app/legacy/` exemption itself, so this review treats that line as a change under review rather than as a rule.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (up to 8 attempts) and `app/health.py` (up to 3 attempts). Both raise `HTTPError` immediately and retry any other `OSError`. It also adds parametrized tests for both, plus a line in `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:49 — correctness — Cap fetch_inventory retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8` makes `fetch_inventory` call `urlopen(url, timeout=10)` up to 8 times with 1s sleeps in between, about 87s per call. This breaks `docs/review-rules.md:5`: "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." The exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` comes from this same pull request, so it is not existing policy. — During an upstream outage, each caller holds a worker thread for up to 87s, which is the failure the rule at `docs/review-rules.md:6` records. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`, update the `8` in `tests/test_retries.py:10` to match, and remove the exemption line from `docs/review-rules.md:7`, or get it approved separately with a bounded total wait for the nightly-restart case.
